io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.utils.compatibility

Class InventoryCompat

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.utils.compatibility.InventoryCompat

  • public final class InventoryCompat
extends java.lang.Object
    Java-8 universal port: Inventory#getStorageContents() is 1.9+. Reached reflectively, falling back to getContents() on older servers (equivalent for the non-player inventories Slimefun uses it on).

    • Method Detail

      • consumeSlot

        public static void consumeSlot(@Nonnull
                               org.bukkit.inventory.Inventory inventory,
                               int slot,
                               int amount,
                               boolean replaceConsumables)
        Consumes amount from the ItemStack in slot of a real (container-backed) Inventory and writes the decremented - or emptied - result back through Inventory.setItem(int, ItemStack).

        dough's ItemUtils.consumeItem(ItemStack, int, boolean) empties a stack with setAmount(0), but on MC 1.8-1.10 CraftItemStack#setAmount(0) only nulls the mirror's handle and does not clear the backing NMS slot (fixed by Mojang in 1.11+). Consuming the last item of a live container mirror there silently leaves it in place - an infinite duplication. Cloning the slot, consuming the clone, then re-setting the slot rebuilds the NMS slot and behaves identically on every version. Use only on real inventories (dispensers, chests, player inventories), never on the virtual DirtyChestMenu stacks, which are not mirrors and are unaffected.

      • consumeHeldItem

        public static void consumeHeldItem(@Nonnull
                                   org.bukkit.entity.Player player,
                                   @Nullable
                                   org.bukkit.inventory.EquipmentSlot hand,
                                   int amount,
                                   boolean replaceConsumables)
        Consumes amount from the ItemStack held in the given hand and writes the result back through the hand API (HandCompat), for the same 1.8-1.10 setAmount(0) reason as consumeSlot(Inventory, int, int, boolean). The event's item mirror is never mutated; the player's actual hand stack is decremented (or replaced with a consumable leftover / cleared) and set back explicitly, which rebuilds the NMS slot on every version.
